questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: To experience living in a new country, improve my english and be in an international environment.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That previous exchange students had a good experience from there, the courses avalible, and clear information provided from the university webpage. Furthermore the surrounding nature, the cost of living, and that the culture was somewhat familiar to my own.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The only thing that would make my study abroad experience better would be less paperwork. I had to write what feels like a gigantic number of e-mails to both my home university and my host university, regarding avalible courses, change of courses, certificates and housing. In addition I wish that my host university would have been better at giving information about new covid regulations to the international students, as all information about covid regulations seemed to come from the local (Swedish) news.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, and if I couldn't find the information I needed on the webpage, I was able to contact the university both via phone or email

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Met by representatives from the university in the airport, who gave out information and housing keys, as well arranged free busses to the housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Very friendly assistance

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: If you wish, you can get housing through the university, you pay a small fee and then you get a login to a housing portal where you can choose your room with a shared kitchen. Super easy. I heard that it is hard to find housing on your own, if you dont go through the university.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There is no living 'on campus' anyway, but a lot of living 'off campus' areas avalible through the university. 'Ålidhem' seemed to be the most popular place for exchange students to live.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The rooms are in a used condition, but still totally find to live in, if anything breaks you can easily get it replaced with new furniture. The landlords are super friendly and quick with fixing things. Usually the kithcens are clean and has a friendly atmosphere, but of course you can be unlucky and get a less social kitchen. There is profesional cleaning of the common areas once a week.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Instructions on how to registrate was very clear

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You look through an online catalogue of all avalible courses and choose which fits you. Information about when the courses are held is also avalible so you can avoid schedule conflicts. After choosing you wait to see if you are admitted to the course or on a waiting list, if you're not certified to take the course you get an email from the university, and can choose another course.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was clear information on the webpage, and additionally you could call the host university or get a reply over e-mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I originally tried to register for a master level class, but couldn't get it because I was on bachelor level. I got all the classes I wanted on bachelor level, although I was on waiting list for one of the classes up until a week before the class started.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start sending e-mails early if you want to get on a master level class even though you are on bachelor levels, maybe you can convince them. Have patience with the waiting list, and it is possible to registrerer for another class just in case you dont get a spot from the waiting list.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some of the courses were great, others had some issues.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level was in general okay, but for one course it was way too low. The level of complexity in the lab parts was in general pretty low.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Mostly the same, although the host institution had fewer interactive classes and focused mostly on lectures and presentations. Q and A lectures was provided before every exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Immunology, bacterial physiology and pathogenesis, genetics and evolution

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The immunology course was super interesting and gave a good overview, and the professors on the course was super kind and inspiring.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: My bike broke so I had to by a new bike, I used about 1000 dkk in total for bikes.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Less expensive: candy, chocolate, nuts, public transportation (short and long distance), housing, eating out. 
More expensive: Vegetables and alcohol.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They had an amazing place called 'fritidsbanken' where you could rent sport and adventure equipment for free.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was at least three different 'kårhus' (student bars) you could be a member of which had activites, as well as an amazing fitness center, with every possible sport included, located on campus.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Become a member of your student bar, and go to their events and parties. Go to soup and pancake thursdays at the skogis kårhus. Become a member of the fitness center (IKSU). Borrow equipment from 'fritidsbanken' and go on adventure. In winter, ice skate on the lake and go skiing or snow boarding. See the brännboll (rundbold) tournament.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out in nature. Hike in the surrounding nature. Camp in the small huts avalible. Ski or snowboard on the local slope. Have a fika down town. Make a bunfire by Nydala lake and see the northen lights.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The swedish mentally is much like the danish.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Ask them questions about activites to do, talk to your neighbour in class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Swedish people tend to not say directly if anything is bothering them

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The huge culture around fika (cake and coffee). There is always someone who's down for a fika

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Dont be afraid to call or e-mail the host institution if they're slow with things or you have questions. Remember to take advantage of fritidsbanken (free outdoor equipment) and go on adventures. Make sure to see the nothern lights.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I felt like it wasn't necessary for me to buy the books suggested for each course.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social aspect and the amazing nature. Living with a shared kitchen made it super easy to get friends, and there are a lot of international students coming to the university in general, which means there is always an activity or party going on. The nature is incredible, and the northen lights are unbelivable.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The paper work

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
